title: Mapping the second component in a pair
statement: Let $g$ be a function from Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $T_g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be monotone. Suppose a finite Turing machine computes $g$ within time $T_g$, meaning it halts on every input $y$ within $T_g(|y|)$ steps and outputs $g(y)$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $z$, $M$ halts within $c(|z|+1+T_g(|z|))$ steps and outputs the pairing of $a$ with $g(b)$ if the aligned pair parser returns $(a,b)$ on $z$, and outputs the empty word if parsing fails.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine computes $g$ within time $T_g$
replaced:
Let a machine compute the total function $g$ within a monotone time bound
$T_g$. Then there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such
that $M$ computes, within $c\,(n + 1 + T_g(n))$ steps on inputs of length
$n$, the function sending a word that encodes the pair $(a,b)$ under the
self-delimiting pair code to the pair encoding of $(a, g(b))$, and any
malformed word to the empty word.
